data.name: Aliyat
data.gender_notes: Aliyat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'alaa' which means 'to raise, to exalt, to be high, noble, or sublime'. The name Aliyat refers to someone who is exalted or sublime, and carries the connotation of nobility, grace, and gentleness. The name Aliyat carries the meaning “Exalted, Sublime, High, Noble” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Aliyat usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted, sublime, high, noble and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Aliyat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted, Sublime, High, Noble.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aliyat total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aliyat has a rich history in Islamic culture, particularly in the context of the important figures Ali ibn Abi Talib and Fatima al-Zahra, the Prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, and his beloved daughter respectively. The names Ali and Fatima are considered some of the most noble and revered names in Islam, and the names Aliyat and Fatimah (variants of Fatima) share the same root. The name Aliyat carries a sense of dignity, nobility, and high status, making it a respected and honorable name in Muslim communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Aliyat can be seen as a reminder of the divine faith and trust in Allah (God). The idea of being exalted or raised up to a higher plane can be interpreted as a call to spiritual growth and an aspiration to attain nearness to Allah. The name Aliyat can serve as an inspiration to strive for a life of nobility, virtue, and piety, reflecting the divine attributes of grace, mercy, and compassion. Additionally, in Sufism (Islamic mysticism), the concept of being raised up to a higher spiritual level is a central theme, making the name Aliyat a powerful reminder of this journey towards spiritual enlightenment.
